title: House Robber
pattern: DP: rob this house or skip it
statement: `nums[i]` is the money in house `i` along a street. Robbing two **adjacent** houses triggers the alarm. Return the maximum amount you can rob.

example.why: Rob houses 0, 2 and 4: 2 + 9 + 1 = 12. No two of them are neighbours.

idea: Go along the street and let `dp[i]` be the most money obtainable from houses `0 … i`.
For house `i` there are only two choices. **Rob it**: house `i − 1` is then forbidden, so add the best of houses `0 … i − 2`. **Skip it**: keep the best of houses `0 … i − 1`.
`dp[i] = max(dp[i − 2] + nums[i], dp[i − 1])`. The last entry is the answer.

complexity.spaceWhy: The dp array (two variables would do, since only the last two entries are read).

steps.text: Our example: **`nums = [2,7,9,3,1]`**. Each step runs one highlighted line of the code.
With only house 0 available, rob it: 2.

views.title: dp[i] = best loot from houses 0 … i

steps.text: With houses 0 and 1 — neighbours, so only one of them — take the richer: max(2, 7) = **7**.

views.title: dp[i] = best loot from houses 0 … i

steps.text: House 2 holds 9. **Rob it**: house 1 must be skipped, so add the best up to house 0: 2 + 9 = 11. **Skip it**: keep 7. Robbing wins → `dp[2]` = **11**.

views.title: dp[i] = best loot from houses 0 … i

steps.text: House 3 holds 3. **Rob it**: 7 + 3 = 10. **Skip it**: keep 11. Skipping is at least as good → `dp[3]` = **11**.

views.title: dp[i] = best loot from houses 0 … i

steps.text: House 4 holds 1. **Rob it**: house 3 must be skipped, so add the best up to house 2: 11 + 1 = 12. **Skip it**: keep 11. Robbing wins → `dp[4]` = **12**.

views.title: dp[i] = best loot from houses 0 … i

steps.text: The last entry covers the whole street: the most that can be robbed is **12**.

views.title: dp[i] = best loot from houses 0 … i

steps.text: Done — the answer is **`12`**. Rob houses 0, 2 and 4: 2 + 9 + 1 = 12. No two of them are neighbours.
